findings.location: Assumptions and constraints, “The form of a theme” table; Increment B
findings.problem: The stored anchor is specified only as a locator/place plus a hash of its first twelve words. It does not retain the exact start and end of the contiguous span or a hash of the full excerpt. This drifts from theme.md’s specified anchor and makes the promised exact-span validation and reliable re-anchoring ambiguous.
findings.suggestion: Define the anchor schema with a typed part locator, explicit start and end offsets/ranges, heading path, and a full-excerpt hash; make Increment A validate all of them and Increment B test re-anchoring using that full hash.

findings.location: Increment D, “The vocabulary of a book’s field” and Step 2
findings.problem: The production vocabulary check is still not reproducibly defined: “frequent,” “rare,” the corpus scope, tokenization/normalization, thresholds, and the common-word list are deferred to implementation and its Result. A test cannot establish one predetermined behavior from this plan.
findings.suggestion: Specify the complete deterministic vocabulary algorithm and its constants/list source in the plan before implementation, then have the fixture test assert that defined algorithm.

findings.location: Assumptions and constraints (line 77); Completion criterion 6; Increment F
findings.problem: The plan excludes every book without a conversion, including pointer-only books, despite theme.md specifying themes from a pointer-only book’s captured snapshot (marked partial) and the roadmap candidate calling for themes for each book. The library run therefore has no required outcome or report entry for that class.
findings.suggestion: Either include pointer-only books by extracting from their snapshots and marking the themes partial, or explicitly record and justify a scope change in the governing spec/roadmap and require the run report to list them as skipped.

findings.problem: The planned test says a failed support check “leaves the theme unmarked,” but the settled theme form and completion criterion require every non-empty neutral part to carry either a stated or inferred mark. It does not say whether such output is dropped, retained outside a generation, or filed despite being malformed.
findings.suggestion: Specify one outcome for a failed support check—normally drop the affected part/theme and record its reason—and make the schema, extraction behavior, and test agree.

summary: The plan has unresolved anchor, deterministic vocabulary, coverage, and failed-check semantics gaps.
